messages.subject: Problems with g.shell.GGIR()
parts:
Hi all,

I'm having some problems with the g.shell.GGIR function. 

I ran the part1 function separately and now I want to make the rest of analyses. Find the script below.

When I run it, this error is displayed: 
  Error in `[<-`(`*tmp*`, di, fi:(fi + (length(qlevels) - 1)), value = c(0.607811349387544,  : subscript out of bounds

I have tried removing the qlevels argument, then the error displayed is:
  Error in `[<-`(`*tmp*`, di, fi, value = 29.4166666666667) : subscript out of bounds

Could any of you detect anything wrong with the script below?
Any help is highly appreciated, thanks in advance.

Best regards,
Jairo

SCRIPT:

g.shell.GGIR(mode = c(2,3,4,5),
             datadir = datadir, outputdir = outputdir,
             studyname = "ActiveBrains_I",
             f0 = 1, f1 = 208,

             viewingwindow = 1,
             ######

             ######
             metadatadir = metadatadir,
             strategy = 1,
             hrs.del.start = 0,
             hrs.del.end = 0,
             maxdur = 8,
             includedaycrit = 16,
             qlevels = c(0.1,0.2,0.25,0.3,0.4,0.5,0.6,0.7,0.75,0.8,0.9),
             mvpathreshold = c(142.6, 464.6, 201.4, 707.0),
             boutcriter = 0.8,
             idloc = 1,
             do.imp = TRUE,
             epochvalues2csv = TRUE,
             mvpadur = c(1, 5, 10),

             #PART 3: all default values
             ######
             ######
             #PART 4
             ######
             metadatadir = metadatadir,
             loglocation = loglocation,

             includenightcrit = 4,
             relyonsleeplog = TRUE,
             ######
             #PART 5
             ######
             metadatadir = metadatadir,
             strategy = 1,
             hrs.del.start = 0,

             loglocation = loglocation,
             threshold.lig = c(30, 40),

messages.author: 8d92e34685fbc6bd
messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Problems with g.shell.GGIR()
parts:
Hi Jairo, Can you change maxdur to 8 and try again? In your current definition all analyses are clipped to zero days of measurement which triggers the error. Maxdur acts like a maximum measurement duration, all data beyond this point will be ignored, so never use maxdur = 0.
Vincent
